title: A 0.75mm2 407μW Real-Time Speech Audio Denoiser with Quantized Cascaded Redundant Convolutional Encoder-Decoder for Wearable IoT Devices
problem: Real-time audio denoising on wearable IoT devices requires extremely low power consumption and minimal silicon area while maintaining quality comparable to cloud-based processing.
motivation: On-device audio denoising enables consistent performance across platforms and protects user privacy. Efficient hardware implementation of ML models is critical for battery-powered wearable devices operating in real-time.
method: The system builds a neural network with two parts: an encoder that compresses audio and a decoder that expands it while filtering out noise. To minimize power and silicon area, it uses quantization—representing numbers with fewer bits instead of full precision—throughout the network. The design also includes a specialized routing scheme that reduces how often the processing elements need to access the fast on-chip memory by 5-9x, which significantly cuts power consumption.
key_novelty: The core innovation combines quantized neural networks (saving 75% memory) with specialized memory routing (cutting on-chip access 5-9x) to achieve a real-time speech denoiser in just 0.75mm² at 407 microwatts on 28nm silicon.
contributions: Quantized convolutional encoder-decoder for audio denoising
Hardware quantization reducing memory usage by 75%
Specialized PE activation routing reducing memory accesses by 5-9x
Highest PESQ audio quality score vs prior works
limitations: Evaluation on specific audio datasets; generalization to other audio tasks not explored. Single-voltage operation point (0.65V) evaluated.
primary_theme: Ultra-low-power ML accelerator for wearable audio
